Struggling with low self-esteem can feel heavy, and it takes courage to reach out about it. A helpful starting point is talking with a mental health professional—a therapist or counselor can work with you on the thoughts and patterns behind how you see yourself. You can find one through your primary doctor, your insurance provider, or directories like Psychology Today. If cost is a concern, community mental health centers and sliding-scale clinics are worth looking into.

In the meantime, small steps can help. Try noticing your self-critical thoughts and gently questioning them—would you speak to a friend that way? Doing things you're even slightly good at, moving your body, and limiting comparisons on social media can also ease some pressure over time.

Be patient with yourself; changing how you view yourself is a gradual process, not a switch you flip. If these feelings ever become overwhelming or you have thoughts of harming yourself, please reach out to a crisis line or someone you trust right away. You deserve support.
